question.worked_solution:
We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(0.18<Z<1.90).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/d327f2ec77d68a09bf14a378bace0c999eb4f24fd3b115a20328647ad3dd7334.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.18<Z<1.90) & =P(Z<1.90)-P(Z\le 0.18) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.90)-P(Z\le 0.18) \\  & =Φ(1.90)-Φ(0.18).\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.18) & =0.5714 \\ Φ(1.90) & =0.9713\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.18<Z<1.90) & =Φ(1.90)-Φ(0.18) \\  & =0.9713-0.5714 \\  & =0.3999.\end{aligned}
$$
